facts.statement: Acynodon was first described in 1997 and initially placed within the family Alligatoridae.
facts.quote: When first described in 1997, it was placed within the family Alligatoridae.

facts.statement: A. adriaticus is the only species of Acynodon for which articulated postcranial material is preserved in at least two specimens.
facts.quote: A. adriaticus is the only species preserving articulated postcranial material in at least two specimens.

facts.statement: Histological analysis of a specimen's dorsal rib shows a thickened cortical layer and at least 31 Lines of Arrested Growth (LAGs) despite the specimen being somatically immature.
facts.quote: Histological thin sections of a specimen's dorsal rib show a thickened cortical layer, possibly associated with strong aquatic adaptations, and at least 31 Lines of Arrested Growth (LAGs) despite the specimen being a somatically immature individual.

facts.statement: The skull of Acynodon is extremely brevirostral, having a small and broad snout compared to other alligatoroids.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Acynodon es extremadamente brevirostral, teniendo un hocico pequeño y ancho en comparación con otros aligatoroides.

facts.statement: The osteoderms of Acynodon possess a distinctive double keel.
facts.quote: Los osteodermos de Acynodon poseen una distintiva doble quilla.

facts.statement: Acynodon first appeared in the lower Campanian of the Late Cretaceous and disappeared during the mass extinction at the K-T boundary.
facts.quote: Acynodon aparece por primera vez en el Campaniense inferior dentro del Cretácico superior, y desapareció durante la extinción masiva ocurrida en el límite K-T.

facts.statement: The time range for Acynodon is from the Campanian to the Danian, approximately 83.6 to 61.66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Danian (83.6 to 61.66 million years ago)
